question: A drug advertisement reporting a relative risk reduction (RRR) of 50% always means that 50 out of every 100 patients treated will benefit compared to placebo.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct. RRR can be large even when the absolute risk reduction (ARR) is small. Always calculate the number needed to treat (NNT = 1/ARR) to assess clinical significance.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: That is incorrect. Relative risk reduction describes the proportional change in event rates between groups — not the absolute number of patients who benefit. A 50% RRR on a baseline event rate of 2% produces an absolute risk reduction of only 1%, meaning you need to treat 100 patients to prevent one event.
